בדברי הטור אחרי שנדקדק עוד למה הוצרך לכתוב כאן והוה אליל של ישראל ואין לה ביטול וצריך להוליכה לים המלח וכי עדיין לא ידענו דין אליל של ישראל מהו עד כאן. ע"כ נ"ל דכיון דראינו לפי המסקנא בגמרא דבזוזא תליא מילתא קשה לכאורה למה לי משיכה בברייתא כיון דהמשיכה אינה עושה כלום דטעות הוה רק מפני הרואים חשו א"כ ליחוש נמי במעות לחוד דהא לרש"י מעות קונות בעלמא וניחוש גם כאן מפני הרואים שלא ידעו מטעותו וע"כ היה אפשר לומר דבאמת העיקר תלוי במעות והא דנקט התנא אם משנתן לו המעות משך הך משיכה ל"ד אלא כלומר משך ומצא האליל לזה נשמר וכתב שאינו כן אלא העיקר דכל שהוא אם היה יודע שיש אליל בתוך הגרוטאות היה לו קנין לפי הדין אז גזרינן כשיש טעות מפני הרואים שיסברו שידע מהם אבל אם לפי הדין יודע לא גזרינן מפני הרואים באינו יודע וע"כ אם משך לחוד דאז אפילו אם ידע אין כאן קנין על האליל כי בודאי בשעה שמשך כל הגרוטאות לא נתכוין אלא כשיהיו בידו יברר לעצמו מה שמותר לו ויחזיר מה שאסור לו דהיתרא ניחא ליה דליקני דאיסורא לא ניחא ליה כדאמרינן פרק השואל אבל כשנתן כבר המעות בעד כל משקל הגרוטאות אי אפשר לומר כן דודאי אם היה יודע שיש אליל בתוכה ודאי קנאו ומ"ה כשהוא שוגג בדבר בשעת מקח חשו למראית עין והקפידו בזה דוקא כשיש שניהם. וא"ל למה לי משיכה הא במעות לחוד קונה גם כן בידוע וא"כ ניחוש בשוגג מפני הרואים. יש לומר דאף בידוע וקנאו לאליל מכח מעותיו מ"מ כיון שלא בא לידו לא היה צריך להוליכו לים המלח אלא סגי בביטול העובד כוכבים כמו שהוכחנו בסמוך דדוקא בא לידו בעינן ע"כ הוצרך הטור כאן לכתוב שצריך להוליכו לים המלח להורות על מה שכתבתי ושיעור דבריו הלוקח גרוטאות ומצא בשוגג אליל אם עד שלא נתן המעות משך יחזיר ואין לחוש מפני הרואים כיון שעדיין לא נקנה המקח אפילו אם היה יודע שיש שם אליל אבל אם עשה שניהם לא יחזיר כיון שאם היה יודע כבר נקנה וכ"ת משיכה למה לי לזה תירץ דהוה אליל של ישראל וצריך להוליכו כו' כיון שבא לידו ע"כ חשו גם בשוגג וא"ל למה ליה לרבא לאוקמי הברייתא באמת שיש מקח טעות ומפני הרואים ולא מוקי לה ביודע וצריך שניהם כמו שכתבנו דהברייתא אמרה ומצא אליל משמע בשעת מקח לא ידע וע"כ היה לו להתיר בכל גווני כיון שלא ידע מאליל מ"ט אסור כשיש שניהם אלא ע"כ משום הרואים וכפי החלוקה אשר זכרנו. ולפי דברינו נתיישב גם כן מ"ש הטור וכ"כ הרמב"ם והקשה ב"י הא ברייתא ערוכה היא ולפי מה שכתבתי ניחא דקא משמע לן דתרווייהו בעינן ולא סגי במעות לחוד כמו שכתבתי לעיל והכל ניחא בסייעתא דשמיא:
turei_zahav.en: One who buys scrap metal, etc. There is a place in the Tur that needs explanation, and we will explain it with Heaven's help. In a baraita it is stated: if before he gave money he pulled — he returns; and if after he gave money he pulled — he takes it to the Dead Sea; and he wants to prove from this in the Gemara that pulling with a gentile does not acquire; and Rava rejected it — in truth it is a mistaken transaction; rather the first part where he gave money it appears as an idol of Israel; the latter part where he did not give money — not so. And the Tur wrote: if he pulled before he gave money he returns to him, for it was not yet acquired; and if after he gave money he pulled — it was already acquired for him and it is an idol of Israel and has no nullification and must be taken to the Dead Sea; and so the Rambam, etc. And it is wondrous — for we conclude in the Gemara that in every case there is no acquisition from mistaken transaction, only the distinction is because it appears acquired or not. And Mahari Chalav wrote that what the Tur wrote "it was already acquired for him" is according to the viewers' opinion who will think he acquired — for everyone holds it was acquired for him; and it does not settle at all that in truth there is acquisition for a gentile, whether by pulling according to R. Tam or by money according to Rashi, as the Tur wrote below siman 322 — only to satisfy both he wrote there that one should do both pulling and money regarding firstborn; and if so it is impossible to say thus in the Tur's words, which are according to the tanna of the latter baraita who required both here; for if so the baraita is not like Rashi nor like R. Tam; and since the law is that one suffices — why concern ourselves with viewers only when there are both and not with one of them, that they too will say it was acquired for Israel since the Tur tied the prohibition to a place where there is acquisition; besides that the language does not imply so in the Tur; and in Perishah he wrote the Tur truly intended as written in siman 322 and therefore required both — and already rejected because of what we wrote that the Tur's words are the baraita's words; and further he was not precise at all, for necessarily he required both only to be stringent, such as to exempt from firstborn; but not to be lenient; and if so here it would be a leniency from this that he could return if there is not acquisition of both — and this is obviously a void matter; and on the contrary the Tur is stringent when there is one of them, namely in siman 132 — see there because of the reason that pulling acquires regarding measuring for a gentile's vessel and money acquires regarding giving a dinar to a shopkeeper; and how can he say here to be lenient until there are both — rather it is simple this is not so. And what appears to me in the Tur's words: after I was precise further — why did he need to write here "and it is an idol of Israel and has no nullification and must be taken to the Dead Sea" — do we not yet know the law of an idol of Israel until here? In the end it appears to me: since we saw according to the conclusion in the Gemara that the matter depends on money — it is difficult apparently why I need pulling in the baraita, since pulling does nothing, it being a mistake only because of viewers; if so let us also be concerned with money alone, for according to Rashi money acquires in general, and let us be concerned here too because of viewers who will not know of his mistake; and therefore it was possible to say that in truth the essence depends on money; and that which the tanna took "if after he gave him money he pulled" — this pulling is not literal, but rather meaning he pulled and found the idol for this one it was guarded; and he wrote it is not so, but the essence is that whenever if he had known there was an idol in the scrap metal he would have had acquisition by law — then we decree when there is a mistake because of viewers who will think he knew of them; but if by law he knew — we do not decree because of viewers when he did not know; and therefore if he pulled alone — then even if he knew there is no acquisition on the idol, for certainly when he pulled all the scrap metal he intended only that when they are in his hand he will clarify for himself what is permitted and return what is forbidden — permitted he wants to acquire, forbidden he does not want to acquire, as we say in chapter HaSho'el; but when he already gave money for all the weight of the scrap metal — it is impossible to say so, for certainly if he had known there was an idol inside he would certainly have acquired it; and nevertheless when he erred at the time of purchase they were concerned for marit ayin and were stringent in this specifically when there are both. And one can say: why do I need pulling — behold with money alone it also acquires in a known case; and if so let us be concerned in error because of viewers. One can say: even though it is known and he acquired the idol through his money — nevertheless since it did not come to his hand he need not take it to the Dead Sea, but nullification of the gentile suffices, as we proved nearby that specifically "it came to his hand" we require; therefore the Tur needed to write here that it must be taken to the Dead Sea to teach what I wrote; and the measure of his words: one who buys scrap metal and found an idol in error — if before he gave money he pulled he returns and need not be concerned for viewers since the purchase was not yet acquired even if he had known there was an idol there; but if he did both he does not return, since if he had known it was already acquired; and if you say: why do I need pulling for this — answer: it is an idol of Israel and must be taken, etc., since it came to his hand — therefore they were concerned also in error; and one can say: why did Rava need to establish the baraita truly that there is mistaken transaction and because of viewers, and not establish it when he knew and requires both, as we wrote — for the baraita says "and found an idol," implying at the time of purchase he did not know; and therefore it should have been permitted in every case since he did not know of the idol — why is it forbidden when there are both — rather necessarily because of viewers and according to the distinction we mentioned. And according to our words it is also settled what the Tur and Rambam wrote; and Beit Yosef challenged: behold the baraita is arranged; and according to what I wrote it is settled — it teaches us we require both and money alone does not suffice, as I wrote above; and everything is settled with Heaven's help:

mechaber.en: Elilim of a non-Jew: if he cut off the tip of its ear, or the tip of its nose, or the tip of its finger, or if he crushed it in its presence — even though it is not lacking — it is nullified. If he crushed it not in its presence and it is not lacking, or he spat in its presence, urinated in its presence, dragged it, or threw excrement at it, it is not nullified. {Rama: And there are those who say that even nullification by mere statement is nullification; but if he nullified it due to duress, it is not nullified until he does an act upon its body, as was explained (Mordechai, at the beginning of perek Kol HaTzelamim, in the name of Ravyah).}

siftei_kohen.he: באמירה בעלמא. ול"ד למכרה או משכנה דבסמוך דהתם זוזי אנסוהו ב"ח ופסק כן. ובד"מ כתב דשאני התם דלא ידעינן בודאי שבטלו אבל כשבטלו אפילו באמירה בעלמא מהני כדברי המרדכי עד כאן ר"ל דהכא מיירי שאומר שרוצה לבטל לקטוע אזנה או חוטמה וכה"ג אבל התם אינו מבטלו וגם סובר שהקונה לא יבטל ודלא כב"י:
siftei_kohen.en: With a mere statement. And one can say regarding selling or pledging — for nearby there the Bach ruled that they forced him with money; and in Darkei Moshe he wrote that it is different there because we do not know for certain they nullified; but when they nullified, even with a mere statement it is effective, as the Mordechai's words — until here his language: here it deals with one who says he wants to nullify — to cut its ear or nose and the like; but there he does not nullify it and also holds the buyer will not nullify — unlike Beit Yosef:

With a mere statement. Beit Yosef wrote on this: and I wonder from the law of selling or pledging nearby — for it implies even if he sold willingly it is not nullified; and Darkei Moshe wrote it is different there because we do not know for certain they nullified:

turei_zahav.he:
מכרה או משכנה כו'. במשנה איתא מכרה או משכנה ר' אומר ביטל וחכמים אומרים לא ביטל וידוע דהלכה כחכמים ואיכא בגמרא פלוגתא חד אמר בצורף עובד כוכבים מחלוקת אבל בצורף ישראל דברי הכל ביטל וחד אמר בצורף ישראל מחלוקת ופסק הטור לחומרא אפילו בצורף ישראל כחכמים דלא בטיל ורמב"ם פסק כלישנא קמא לקולא בצורף ישראל וכתב הר"ן טעמו מדאיתא אח"כ בברייתא ת"ר לוה עליה או שנפלה עליה מפולת כו' אינה בטילה וצריכא דאי תנא לוה עליה הייתי אומר מדלא זבנה לא ביטלה ש"מ מהאי ברייתא דזבנה מהני והיינו ע"כ בצורף ישראל ואתיא כרבנן מ"ה מהני מכרה אבל לוה עליה לא וכתב הר"ן הא דבטל במשכנו לרבי דוקא בהרהינו למשכון אצלו ואמר אי לא אפדנו לזמן פלוני יהא שלך והגיע הזמן ולא פדאו אז דוקא בטל לרבי דחשוב כמכירה וממילא הוה לדידן כן הלכה בצורף ישראל לרמב"ם וב"י חלק על הר"ן וכתב דבמשכון אין חילוק בין הרהין או לא דאפילו הרהין המשכון לצורף ישראל לא בטלה והוכיח כן מדלא נקט בגמרא גבי לוה עליה מדלא הרהינו ולמה נקט מדלא זבנה אלא דבמשכן לא איכפת לן בהרהין או לא וכתב שכ"מ מדברי הרמב"ם ונרא' דמשמע ליה כן ברמב"ם מדכתב וז"ל מכרו לישראל צורף בטלה משכנו או מכרו לעובד כוכבים או לישראל שאינו צורף לא בטלה עד כאן לשונו מדלא נקט ברישא אלא מכירה לחוד ש"מ משכון ע"י הרהון לא מהני ולפ"ז יהיו דברי הרמב"ם בסיפא לצדדין וה"ק אבל משכנו אפילו לישראל צורף או מכרו לאינו צורף לא בטלה ולפ"ז קשה למה כתב כאן ויש מתירין בצורף ישראל דמשמע גם במשכנו. ומו"ח ז"ל כתב ג"כ דהאי פסקא דש"ע ביש מתירין ליתא במשכנו אבל תמיהני על הב"י שהרי אמרינן בגמרא אבל בצורף ישראל דברי הכל בטל דהיינו שמודים חכמים לרבי ור' נקט בפירוש משכנו או שמכרו במתני' והיאך נימא שלא הודו לו אלא במכרו ולעשות מחלוקת חדשה במשכנו אפילו בצורף ישראל אין ביטול לחכמים אלא ודאי דברי הר"ן עיקר דבמשכון דמתני' דהיינו הרהינו מודים חכמים לרבי דבטל וברייתא דלוה עליה אינו בטל מיירי בלא הרהין ומיירי בישראל צורף ואתיא כרבנן ודוקא לוה עליה הלואה בעלמא אבל אם הרהינו אצלו על זמן ולא פדאו הוה כמכר גמור כמ"ש בא"ח סימן תמ"א בחמצו של ישראל ביד עובד כוכבים ולא הוצרך התלמוד להזכיר כאן מדלא זבנה וממילא גרע זה דהיינו מכירה ממש ומתניתין דנקטה משכנה מיירי בהרהינו אצלו וע"כ בטל לרבי אפילו בצורף עובד כוכבים וא"ל למה הוצרך למתני כלל משכנה כיון דאמרינן דהוה כמכירה לא קשה מידי דכיון דהצורף עובד כוכבים במתניתין סלקא דעתיך אמינא שהממשכנה לא ביטלה דמימר אמר אותו העובד כוכבים שהלוה לי (עשה) יחוס עליה ולא ישברנה קמשמע לן דאפ"ה בטלה לרבי אבל בברייתא בצורף ישראל לא שייך לומר כן פשיטא דהרהינה כמכירה ממש ומש"ה שפיר כתב הרמב"ם ברישא דבטל היינו במכירה ולא זכר שם משכנה כדי שלא תטעה לומר אפילו משכון בעלמא בלא הרהין אבל באמת הרהינה הוה מכר גמור ומהני בצורף ישראל ובסיפא דמיירי בשל עובד כוכבים כתב גם משכנה דרך לא זו אף זו דכל משכון לא מהני ואפילו הוה כמו מכירה דמכירה עצמה גם כן לא מהני. והנה בכסף משנה כתב הרב בפשיטות להסכים עם הר"ן וכך הם דבריו פה בשלחן ערוך ויש מתירין דהיינו אפילו במשכנו דהיינו שהרהינו אצלו והגיע הזמן ולא פדאו ודבר זה היה לו להרב לכתוב כאן בשלחן ערוך ולבאר באיזה משכון מתירין דהיינו בהרהינו ולא פדאו בזמנו כן נראה לע"ד ברור ועיקר:
ומשמשי עבודת כוכבים אם משכנו כו'. נ"ל פשוט דגם האי משכנו הוא בהרהינו אצלו לזמן ולא פדאו כמו לעיל אבל משכון סתם לא מהני לבטל.
turei_zahav.en:
He sold or pledged it, etc. In the mishnah it is stated: he sold or pledged it — Rabbi says nullified and the Sages say not nullified; and it is known the halachah is like the Sages; and there is a dispute in the Gemara: one says with a gentile smith there is a dispute, but with an Israelite smith all agree it is nullified; and one says with an Israelite smith there is a dispute; and the Tur ruled stringently — even with an Israelite smith, like the Sages who say it is not nullified; and the Rambam ruled like the first version — leniently with an Israelite smith; and the Ran wrote his reason: since afterwards in a baraita it is taught: if he borrowed on it or a collapse fell on it, etc. — it is not nullified; and it is necessary: for if it taught "he borrowed on it" I would say since he did not sell it, it is not nullified — learn from this baraita that selling helps; and this is necessarily with an Israelite smith, and it is like the Rabbis; if so selling helps but borrowing on it — no; and the Ran wrote: that which it is nullified when he pledged it — for Rabbi specifically when he pledged it as collateral with him and said "if I do not redeem by such-and-such time it shall be yours" and the time arrived and he did not redeem — then specifically it is nullified for Rabbi, considered like a sale; and automatically for us the halachah is likewise with an Israelite smith for the Rambam; and Beit Yosef disagreed with the Ran and wrote that in a pledge there is no distinction whether pledged or not — even pledged to an Israelite smith it is not nullified; and he proved thus because the Gemara regarding "he borrowed on it" did not take "he did not pledge it," and why did it take "he did not sell it" — rather in a pledge we do not care whether pledged or not; and he wrote that so several places from the Rambam's words; and it appears he understands thus in the Rambam, for he wrote: "he sold it to an Israelite smith — nullified; he pledged it or sold it to a gentile or to an Israelite who is not a smith — not nullified" — until here his language; from that he did not take at the beginning only selling alone — learn that pledge through collateral does not help; and accordingly the Rambam's latter words are on two sides: and meaning: but if he pledged it, even to an Israelite smith, or sold to one who is not a smith — not nullified; and accordingly it is difficult why he wrote here "and some permit with an Israelite smith" — implying also in pledging. And Mahari Chalav also wrote that this ruling of Shulchan Aruch "some permit" does not exist in pledging; but I wonder at Beit Yosef — for we say in the Gemara "but with an Israelite smith all agree it is nullified" — meaning the Sages agree with Rabbi; and Rabbi explicitly took pledging or selling in the mishnah — and how can we say they did not agree with him except in selling, and make a new dispute in pledging that even with an Israelite smith there is no nullification for the Sages? Rather certainly the Ran's words are primary: in the mishnah's pledge, namely when he pledged it as collateral — the Sages agree with Rabbi that it is nullified; and the baraita "he borrowed on it" is not nullified deals without collateral and deals with an Israelite smith and is like the Rabbis; and specifically "he borrowed on it" — ordinary borrowing; but if he pledged it with him for a time and did not redeem it — it is like a complete sale, as written in Orach Chaim siman 441 regarding chametz of an Israelite in a gentile's hand; and the Talmud did not need to mention here "he did not sell it" — and automatically this is worse, namely an actual sale; and the mishnah that took pledging deals when pledged with him — therefore it is nullified for Rabbi even with a gentile smith; and one can say: why did the mishnah need to teach pledging in general, since we say it is like selling — there is no difficulty, for since the gentile smith in the mishnah comes to your mind, I might think the one who pledged is not nullified — for that gentile will say "the one who lent to me had regard for it and will not break it" — it teaches us that nevertheless it is nullified for Rabbi; but in the baraita with an Israelite smith it is not relevant to say so — obviously pledging is like an actual sale; and therefore the Rambam properly wrote at the beginning it is nullified, namely in selling, and did not mention pledging there so one not err to say even an ordinary pledge without collateral; but in truth pledging was a complete sale and helps with an Israelite smith; and in the latter part dealing with gentile property he also wrote pledging — a way of "not only this but also that," for any pledge does not help, and even if it were like selling — selling itself also does not help. And behold in Kesef Mishneh the Rav wrote plainly to agree with the Ran; and such are his words here in Shulchan Aruch "and some permit" — meaning even in pledging, namely when he pledged it with him and the time arrived and he did not redeem; and the Rav should have written this here in Shulchan Aruch and explained in what pledge they permit, namely with collateral and he did not redeem on time — so it appears clear to me, and the Ran's words are primary:
And the work of stars if they were built. A simple model of the island of his neighbor is at his mercy for time and not as pedagogical as above, but he is just not willing to cancel.

And there's a quaint. It is written in the name of the Lord and his wife, and he has been called, and has not been named after the Lord, and he has written his name:
With a smith, etc. Rashi there on "an unnamed, etc."; and Tosafot there on "but" wrote that a smith — no; but the Rambam, Raavad, and Ramban wrote that specifically a smith; but one who is not a smith — according to him it is not nullified, whether with a gentile, Israel, Rabbi, or the Rabbis; and see there in the Ran:

turei_zahav.en: Since he nullified one limb, etc. Beit Yosef explained the Rambam's intent — Marya dehai pesika — who challenged him from what we hold in the dispute of Rav and Shmuel at the beginning of chapter All Images, whom Beit Yosef brings regarding an idol that broke by itself — that an ordinary person cannot restore it, and it is nullified for all; and above chapter 25 Rav and R. Yochanan dispute and we hold like R. Yochanan stringently; therefore the Rambam resolved: Rav and Shmuel do not dispute where an ordinary person cannot restore it and it is permitted — they do not speak without nullification; rather in any case nullification of one of them is required, namely we consider them as if still in their completeness since it broke by itself; and if a gentile nullified even one of its limbs — so too it helps now; but where an ordinary person can restore it — each piece is by itself an idol; therefore each piece must be nullified by itself; but in the Tur he wrote here that if an ordinary person cannot restore it — it is nullified; and on this it is certainly difficult — behold we hold like R. Yochanan that what broke by itself is not nullified; and it appears the Tur also holds like the resolution Beit Yosef brought in the name of Ramban and Ran that there is a distinction whether the idol's essence remains or not; therefore above in the dispute of Rav and R. Yochanan it deals where the essence remains, only a little broke from it for nullification if the gentile did so — we hold it is not nullified since it broke by itself; and in this it is not relevant to say at all whether an ordinary person can restore it or not, for the gentile does not seek to restore it since its essence remains and he worships it as at first; unlike in the dispute of Rav and Shmuel it deals where all of it broke — and this is explained in what they said "an ordinary person can restore it" — evidently its worship is void as long as it is not restored; in this the Tur properly ruled where it cannot be restored — it is nullified even if it broke by itself, for certainly the gentile nullified it after he saw all of it broke; and one can say: why did the Tur not write the law where its essence remains — one can say we learn from what the Tur wrote where an ordinary person cannot restore it — it is nullified when it broke by itself; automatically we know where restoration is not needed, namely where its essence remains — it is forbidden when it broke by itself, as above; the Tur's view is correct:

turei_zahav.he: ולכנות לה שם גנאי. כתוב בפריש' בשם רש"ל פי' דוקא בא"י והוא תימה ונראה דט"ס הוא כאן ושייך על הרישא דצריך לשרש אחריה דזו דוקא בא"י שצריך להיות מנוקה ומטוהרת שוב ראיתי כן ברמב"ם פ"ח בפי' ובח"ל אין אנו מצווים לרדוף אחריה אלא כל מקום שנכבוש נאבד כל אליל שבו עכ"ל:
turei_zahav.en: Prepare for her a jealous name. It is written in the name of Rashi in the name of Rashi, and it is written in the name of the Lord, that it is written in the name of the Lord, that it is necessary for him to be saved by the Lord, that we should be cleansed and purified again, that I have seen the blessing of the Lord, and we are not commanded to pursue it, but any place that is occupied by any place that we shall be lost

baer_heitev.he: ולכנות. כ' הט"ז דרש"ל פי' דוקא בא"י והוא תימה ונראה דט"ס הוא כאן ושייך על הרישא דצריך לשרש אחריה זו דוקא בא"י וכן הוא לשון הרמב"ם ובח"ל אין אנו מצוים לרדוף אחריה וכו' עכ"ל (ובנה"כ כ' דאין כאן ט"ס וכן משמע בש"ס דהא דצריך לשרש אחריה ולכנות לה וכו' ילפינן מחד קרא ואבדתם וגו' מן המקום ההוא וכי היכי דצריך לשרש הוא דוקא בא"י ה"ה לכנות וכו' ג"כ אינו אלא בא"י עכ"ל):
baer_heitev.en: And to name it. The Taz wrote that Rashi explained specifically in Eretz Yisrael — and this is wondrous; and it appears there is a scribal error here and it applies to the beginning that one must uproot it — this is specifically in Eretz Yisrael; and so is the Rambam's language; and in chutz la'aretz we are not commanded to pursue it, etc. — end. (And in Nekudot HaKesef he wrote there is no scribal error here; and so it implies in the Talmud: that which one must uproot it and name it, etc. — we derive from one verse "and you shall destroy, etc., from that place"; and just as uprooting is specifically in Eretz Yisrael — so too naming is only in Eretz Yisrael — end.)
